import bisect


def k_machine_schedule(jobs: list[list[int]], k: int) -> int:
    if not jobs:
        return 0

    # Sort by end time so we can compute the latest compatible job for each one
    items = sorted(jobs, key=lambda j: j[1])
    ends = [j[1] for j in items]
    n = len(items)

    # p[i] = number of jobs (among the first i in sorted order) that end
    # at or before items[i-1]'s start, i.e. the last compatible job index
    prev = [bisect.bisect_right(ends, items[i][0]) for i in range(n)]

    # dp[c][i] = max pay using at most c machines on the first i jobs
    # Each machine's schedule is a chain of non-overlapping jobs, so we
    # compute the best for c machines by choosing whether to include job i-1
    # on one of the machines (it may follow any chain ending at prev[i-1]).
    # Using the classic k-machine weighted interval DP:
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(k + 1)]

    for c in range(1, k + 1):
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            skip = dp[c][i - 1]
            take = dp[c - 1][prev[i - 1]] + items[i - 1][2]
            dp[c][i] = max(skip, take)

    return dp[k][n]
